evidence.title: Current project deliverable register
evidence.body:
Record signed project scope: Signed purchase scope, equipment boundary, customer contacts, milestone budget and change delegation recorded; no predicted savings are treated as earned revenue.
Verify site survey and customer constraints: Survey records equipment position, rigging route, electrical tie-in, meter/CT locations, customer operations restrictions and the network owner. Qualified engineers determine actual design values.
Issue project design package: Responsible engineer issues the current single-line, equipment layout and interfaces, with source documents and unresolved review comments indexed. A draft or email acknowledgement is insufficient.
Record applicable permit review: Record building/electrical review and separate fire-review acceptance for this project and current drawing revision. A submission receipt does not close either review.
Record pre-install utility review: Record the applicable utility pathway, accepted application and installation-stage conditions; this does not grant operating authorization.
Confirm ordered equipment and shipping record: Supplier confirms ordered configuration, shipping record and remaining equipment documentation. An arrival estimate is distinct from facility receiving evidence.
Verify pad, access and site readiness: EPC attests pad, route and laydown readiness, working access and the agreed delivery interface. Construction details remain the responsibility of qualified site personnel.
Unload and position battery equipment: Receiving contact verifies delivered equipment against the order and visible receiving exceptions; the rigging crew separately confirms its slot and completes placement.
Electrical tie-in during customer window: Electrical contractor uses issued drawings and separately confirmed crew/customer access. Customer operations authorizes the interruption and operating contingency; availability is not that authorization.
Verify installation against issued design: Qualified verifier compares the installation with current drawings and records terminations, conductors, grounding, metering/CT orientation and protection-setting checks. Defects require installer correction and qualified reinspection; the assistant supplies no engineering settings.
Run and record operational commissioning tests: Controls engineer records operational functional tests after network, field, inspection and operating-authority gates. Applicable utility witness/acceptance tests belong to the earlier utility authorization package and may precede that authorization. Network reachability alone does not demonstrate correct meter readings or battery/control behavior.
Issue as-built and support document pack: Issue the revision-controlled as-built single-line and layout, installation/inspection records, equipment serial and warranty index, and site emergency/support contacts.
Record customer monitoring walkthrough: Customer operations confirms the monitoring walkthrough, contact/escalation route and operating responsibility handoff; this does not establish savings performance.
Complete monitoring and customer handoff: Fleet engineer accepts current equipment/configuration index, telemetry sample, alert routing and named support owner after customer training and as-built records. Program eligibility/enrollment is recorded separately and not inferred from physical installation.

evidence.title: Project-specific demo assumptions
evidence.body:
Synthetic project with recorded installation completion; physical work and all completion records are simulated.
A customer firewall connectivity failure is already observed; customer IT owns the network fix and controls owns subsequent functional testing.
Qualified field verification and utility operating acceptance are separate outstanding gates; a receipt cannot authorize operation.
The target is November 23 handoff after November 18 verification and November 20 controls commissioning.
Posted-to-date costs are illustrative invoices at the opening snapshot; task completion does not automatically manufacture new invoices.
Municipal and utility paths are synthetic case assumptions, not verified Worcester requirements or a verified service-territory assignment.
